Royal

ROY-uhl · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Royal is belonging to or relating to a king or queen.

The royal crown sparkled with rubies and pearls.

Worked Example

The royal family waved from the palace balcony.

The family lives in a palace and includes the king and queen. Things that belong to kings and queens are royal.

How Royal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

kingly

kingly: like a king

regal

regal: grand, like royalty

Antonyms

common

common: belonging to ordinary people

ordinary

ordinary: normal, nothing special

How Strong Is It? — Fancy → royal → Majestic

Fancy vs. royal

Fancy vs. royal: Fancy is milder: a fancy chair just has gold paint on it.

Majestic vs. royal

Majestic vs. royal: Majestic is grander still: the coronation was a majestic event that filled the whole cathedral.

The pieces

root — roy

root — roy: king (Old French (roi))

suffix — al

suffix — al: characteristic of, relating to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Roy- comes from an old French word for king, so royal means having to do with kings and queens.

Use the root in a new word: royalty

Use the root in a new word: royalty: The museum's crown jewels once belonged to royalty. (Royalty is simply the noun form of royal - it names kings, queens, and their families as a group.)
